name: Dígne
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Dígne, also called Dige, Dighe, and Duibne, was an Irish goddess. She governed the land of Munster in southeast Ireland. Later writers merged her with the hag goddess Cailleach. The Dingle peninsula in County Kerry bears her name. Writers point to the peninsula as one of Ireland's most scenic areas. Inscriptions in ogham writing found there carry Dígne's name. Because of those inscriptions, scholars interpret her as the ancestral goddess of the region. Her link to the peninsula ties her to local land and to an early writing system.

okr.objective: Identify Dígne as the ancestral goddess of Munster and explain her link to the Dingle peninsula.
